Listen to this article Share A solar-powered greenhouse initiative in Enugu is expected to create and improve employment opportunities for 17,000 young people, particularly women, through increased participation in agriculture and agrifood businesses. The initiative, implemented under the Energising Women and Youths in Agrifood Systems (EWAS) programme, is a partnership between the Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet (GEAPP) and the Mastercard Foundation. Officials from both organisations visited a greenhouse facility operated by MANAMUS Electric at Ugwuomu-Nike, in Enugu East local government area, on Monday to assess the project’s activities and its potential to expand employment opportunities in the agricultural value chain. Chianda Njogu, director of Powering Opportunity in Africa at GEAPP, said the partnership with the Mastercard Foundation was designed to improve livelihoods and expand access to decent work for young people, particularly women. Read also: UNIDO, global leaders’ new book focuses on industrialisation, job creation “We’ve partnered the Mastercard Foundation to create and improve jobs and livelihoods for 17,000 youth, particularly young women. This is part of a larger programme called Energising Women and Youths in Agrifood Systems,” Njogu said. Njogu explained that the programme extends beyond Nigeria to Ethiopia, while implementation in Nigeria is supported by partners including RMI and MANAMUS Electric. He said GEAPP’s broader objective was to address energy poverty, but emphasised that expanding electricity access was only one part of the intervention. The alliance also wants to ensure that reliable energy translates into productive economic activities, employment and improved living standards. Read also: How job creation in Nigeria can translate to decent work “The most important outcome we’re expecting is how to create and improve jobs and livelihoods, and how to create economic prosperity for countries and communities,” Njogu said. The greenhouse project demonstrates how renewable energy can support agricultural production while opening up employment opportunities for young people and women. By integrating solar power into farming operations, the initiative seeks to connect energy access with food production, enterprise development and improved livelihoods.
